reason: Issues #115-117 found during review of #114: reject overflowing integer operations and out-of-range literal magnitudes; preserve each finite next strength when merging or rebuilding. Keep the approved strict-endpoint guard and all frozen records unchanged; rebind sources additively.
literal_rule: Decimal magnitudes up to INT64_MAX are ordinary integers. Magnitude INT64_MAX+1 is accepted only directly after unary minus (whitespace, comments and leading zeros allowed), producing INT64_MIN. A positive magnitude in parentheses remains out of range; negating INT64_MIN is checked overflow.

arithmetic_audit.eval_int: Checked add/subtract/multiply; negation uses checked 0-a. Division/remainder reject zero and INT64_MIN/-1 before executing. Set sizes are uint32_t and bus widths use validated uint16_t endpoints, so their conversions and width arithmetic fit int64_t.
arithmetic_audit.eval_int_reduction: Check every sum/product accumulation, including intermediate overflow before a later cancellation or zero.
arithmetic_audit.eval_set/eval_domain: Check stepped-range stride subtraction; keep the guarded step increment, strict-endpoint shifts and inclusive-domain increment from #114.
arithmetic_audit.pre_indexed_x: Merge only representable nonnegative counts with equal strengths; preserve the outer strength when an inner rewrite forces reconstruction. Zero count remains the identity. Mixed chains keep the strength at each position.
